elements.content: Grammar focus: Future Continuous.

Fix the future moment first, then decide whether the action will be in progress or completed. In progress: will be plus -ing. Completed: will have plus the participle. Use the continuous for polite enquiries about plans, which asks what someone will be doing rather than what they have decided.

will be + -ing — in progress at a future point: at ten, we will be presenting
time phrase — fixes the point: this time tomorrow
negative — won't be + -ing: they won't be working on Friday
question — will + subject + be + -ing: will you be using the room?
polite enquiry — softens the question: will you be joining us?
contrast with future perfect — in progress versus completed: will be finishing / will have finished
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'At nine, she ___ the opening speech.'
2. Complete: '___ you be using the car tonight?'
3. Which sentence means the action will be finished by then?
options: We will have finished by ten.
We will be finishing at ten.

elements.content: Read and listen: three examples in context.

At ten, we will be presenting. — In progress at ten. (Will be + -ing.)
This time tomorrow, I will be travelling. — In progress at that moment. (Time phrase fixes the point.)
Will you be using the room at three? — Polite enquiry about a plan. (Question form.)
What do you observe?

The future continuous describes an action that will be in progress at a future moment. It is built with will be plus the -ing form, and it usually comes with a time expression (at ten, this time tomorrow, at three). It also softens an enquiry about someone's plans, and it presents a future event as a matter of course rather than as a decision.
1. What does the future continuous describe?
options: An action in progress at a future point.
An action finished by a future point.

elements.content: 2. Why use it in 'Will you be using the room at three?'
options: It makes the question more indirect.

Success criteria:
- I can use will be + -ing for an action in progress.
- I can fix the moment with a time phrase.
- I can use it for a polite enquiry about plans.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ At ten, we will presenting (missing be after will) → ✅ At ten, we will be presenting
❌ This time tomorrow I will be travel (base verb instead of -ing) → ✅ This time tomorrow I will be travelling
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

At noon, the auditors will be checking the accounts.
Will you be attending the briefing?
We won't be accepting new bids until March.

- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
